# Finite-wave-vector order, q stars and supercells

This module converts a commensurate wave vector to a stepwise checkable real-space pattern, then calculates surviving operations, translation domains, and Fourier weights in browser Python/NumPy.

## Explicit model scope

- The parent lattice is a square layer with one scalar mode per site; planar coordinates are embedded in three dimensions.
- Declared N×N supercells with N=2,3,4 contain 4,9,16 sites.
- Parent finite periodic  quotient group  `G=(Z_N×Z_N)⋊C4v` contains 8N² abstract operations.
- Modes can represent occupancy deviations or out-of-plane displacement amplitudes unchanged in sign by these C4v operations. Horizontal mirrors, inversion and axial-moment representations are excluded.
- No arbitrary 3D space-group irrep, standard-label, or incommensurate superspace classification. A specified-amplitude pattern does not establish real-material stability.

At N=2, different abstract operations share four-site permutations. Retain identities; this non- faithful representation  still obeys multiplication/orbit– stabilizer .

## Inputs and conventions

Calculation entry `wavevector_lab`, Python `wavevector_lab.calculate(payload)`.

|Input|Default|Meaning|
| --- | --- | --- |
| period | 4 | Side length N of the declared supercell; 2, 3 or 4 |
| qx,qy | 1,0 | Integer wave-vector numerators, −4 to 4, reduced modulo N |
|pattern|single|single activates input-q conjugate pair; multi all star pairs|
| amplitude | 1 | Real amplitude of the input conjugate pair, −5 to 5 |
| transverseRatio | 1 | Other conjugate-pair amplitudes relative to the first, −3 to 3 |
|phaseDegrees|0|First-pair phase,−360…360°|
| relativePhaseDegrees | 0 | Phase of other conjugate pairs relative to the first, −360 to 360 degrees |

Actual q in parent reciprocal units is `(qx/N,qy/N,0)`. Sites are ordered x-fast, then y. Active `(R,t)` maps r to `Rr+t mod N`; fields transform as `D(g)f(r)=f(g⁻¹r)`. The input conjugate pair is listed first, followed deterministically by others.

Each active pair adds `A cos(2πq·r+φ)`. Nonselfconjugate pairs have cos/sin modes. If `q≡−q`, sin vanishes everywhere; phase only multiplies the unique real amplitude by cosφ. Do not use “two distinct satellites each A²/4 intensity.”

## What is actually calculated

1. Rotate q with eight integer point operations and deduplicate modulo reciprocal vectors to obtain its full star.
2. Pair q/−q, build/orthogonalize real Fourier bases for full stars.
3. Superpose pairs using input amplitudes and phases to obtain the actual field.
4. Enumerate all 8N² supercell operations and directly compare permuted/original fields to find stabilizer H.
5. Deduplicate fields under parent/pure translations to obtain all related patterns/translation domains.
6. Find compatible rectangular periods from nonzero Fourier components and compute the minimum translation index exactly from the translation stabilizer.
7. Use the negative-exponent 2D DFT normalized by 1/N² to obtain complex coefficients, relative weights, and Parseval residuals.

 stabilizer  uses relative-to-max tolerance 10⁻⁹, after clearing trig roundoff at 10⁻¹³ of input amplitude. Tiny nonzero amplitudes are not mistaken for zero by fixed absolute thresholds. Near special phases/amplitudes,  stabilizer  labels mean within tolerance.

### Why two supercell descriptions differ

`rectangularPeriod=[Lx,Ly]` is a compatible period along original x,y. `translationIndex=N²/|H∩T|` is the area index of actual surviving translations. For N=3,q=(1,1)/3, a single-q pattern preserves `(1,−1)`, giving rectangular 3×3 but minimal index 3. The rectangular cell is not claimed minimal oblique, and no general primitive reconstruction is returned.

### Why domain counts differ

`domainCount=|G|/|H|` includes every distinct pattern generated by parent operations, including orientations. `translationDomainCount=|T|/|H∩T|` counts only antiphase patterns obtained by translating the current pattern. No energies or domain-wall dynamics are calculated.

### Physical limitations of Fourier weights

`spectrum` is scalar-modulation DFT. Generic nonselfconjugate single-q cosines have A/2 coefficients at two distinct  reciprocal lattice  points. Overall phases change coefficient phases, not intensities; selfconjugate points are separate.

It is not a complete experimental diffraction cross section: atomic form factors, atomic bases, displacement-scattering Q·u factors, magnetic polarization and instrument geometry are omitted. Occupancy deviations also lack a background value ensuring physical occupation fractions.

## Interaction and lessons

-7 presets: four-period single-q, equal double-q, checkerboard, three-period general phase, unequal quarter-phase, three-period oblique stripes, and two-period project stripes.
- 3 lessons: constructing real representations from q; supercells and stabilizers; Fourier satellites and prediction verification.
- Each lesson has 4 derivation steps, 12 total; plus 2 predict-then-verify questions.
-3 atlas cases state assumptions and connect transitions,  domain wall , diffraction,  dynamic structure factor .
- `replay` shows actual rotations, real bases, superpositions, translations and projection reconstructions.
- `subgroupGraph` builds actual inclusion of exact member sets G,T,H,H∩T,identity, merging identical sets.
- `grading` gives complete q-star subspace tasks≤16 rows, allowing phases, normalization, invertible internal  change of basis . Target full representation spaces, not one pattern.

## Result fields

Standard outputs: `summary`,`tables`,`plots`,`checks`,`warnings`,`formulaLinks`. `wavevector` adds `star`,`pairs`,`field`,`sites`,`points`,`basis`,`projector`,`spectrum`,`operations`,`domains`,`translationDomains`, plus these orders, periods, and domain counts.

Complex arrays use `{re,im}`. All outputs are native JSON-serializable; no servers/new Python dependencies.

## Validation

Run `python scripts/test-python-wavevector.py`.

Twelve tests cover group multiplication/associativity for all supported supercells, permutation homomorphisms, every q Fourier subspace, stabilizers under direct coordinate action, cosets/domain counts, direct DFT, Parseval, phase/translation, self-conjugate arms, zero/tiny fields, true subgroup inclusion, internal basis changes, all presets, and invalid inputs.

## Original/official references

- [ISODISTORT official help](https://iso.byu.edu/isodistorthelp.php): a more general framework for structural modes, wave vectors, order-parameter directions and domains.
- [Campbell et al., ISODISPLACE, J. Appl. Cryst. 39,607–614 (2006)](https://doi.org/10.1107/S0021889806014075): original known-parent distortion-mode construction. This finite square model does not replace the complete program.
- [NumPy DFT conventions](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/routines.fft.html): negative exponent, normalization, real-data conjugation.
